So he had to let them go. They were taken out at the checkpoint, as I said, and that was the last that was heard about them. That doctor who treated them at the health centre, who was responsible for them, was Nenad Davidovic. The other patients, in addition to Ismet Nalic, were Omic Hasan and a man named Karadzic whose first name I can't remember. It was Almaz, Almaz Karadzic. They are still registered as missing and we haven't learned anything about them to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ismet Nalic was your father-in-law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After he was expelled from the Mahala, he was living with me at my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you heard this account from Mr. Rajko Kriska of what happened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the driver of the official ambulance belonging to the health centre marked visibly with a red cross on its sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Carakova is in the municipality of Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kriska identify the three Serbian soldiers who stopped the ambulance? Did he know who they were?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately he didn't tell me that. He just said three Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 709. And I want to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to direct your mind back to the events in Sanski Most in connection with the movement of the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown the B/C/S version of this document. There's only one paragraph that interests me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, witness?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 1 and you look at the third paragraph, you will see that it states: "There are currently about 18.000 Muslims and Croats in the Sanski Most municipality area, and in order to avoid danger to the Serbian people it is necessary to organise their voluntary resettlement." Now, you can see that this is a conclusion of the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly. Do you see that? If you look at the top of this document.

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: President of the executive board, Mladen Lukic. Yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the first paragraph of this document, the paragraph at the very top, indicate the date on which this particular matter was discussed at the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't quite understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll lead you straight to it. You can see in the very first paragraph of this document that it states that the municipal assembly at its ninth session held on the 27th of July of 1992 adopted a number of conclusions. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of those conclusions is what I've just read out to you, that 18.000 Muslims and Croats need to be resettled from Sanski Most. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall having a meeting with Mr. Vlado Vrkes and other Serbian leaders in Sanski Most on the 28th of July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Of course I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what was discussed at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to explain if you allow me the reason why this meeting was convened in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BESIM ISLAMCEVIC
utterances.text: The night before -- that is, the night between the 26th and the 27th -- an attack was orchestrated on Podbrijezje, an attack from the neighbouring commune of Podlug from about half past 10.00 p.m. until half past 9.00 in the morning you could hear shooting of about even intensity, I would say. It was a very long night. We could hardly wait for the light of dawn to be able to see what it was all about. We could see hay burning in stables and a couple of roofs here and there. Nobody left their house. Everybody was too afraid. And that was the reason why we requested a meeting with Mr. Vrkes. And on that day, at 1.30 p.m., I called a well-respected Serb citizen in Sanski Most whom I knew and who worked at the Secretariat for the Interior in Sanski Most to ask for his help, and I complained to him that I was not able to cross the checkpoint. I told him I needed someone to come and let us through -- lead us through, rather. The gentleman I called was in fact Dusko Radic. Around half past 1.00 a police car arrived before my house and took me to a meeting with Vlado Vrkes at the police department. I was not the only person there to meet him. I found Mr. Branko Davidovic there, a former president of the municipality, a lawyer by the name of Dosenovic, another man called Rajkica, who was also a lawyer, and some other people who worked at the Secretariat for the Interior. I asked Vrkes "What was this in Podbrijezje all about?" And I have to tell you the truth about his answer. He said, "Forget about that. That's nothing serious. It's a fake attack." There was a part -- an area to the north of Podbrijezje called Bojancici from which several bursts of gunfire were fired towards our neighbours, and that was enough to alarm the citizens of Podbrijezje and to start the shooting. That same night a civilian deputy in charge of Podbrijezje, Mr. Pero Nikolic, left my house, and strangely enough he said absolutely nothing about this. But I had a telephone number of the community centre in Podlug, and in desperation I dialed it several times to try to find out what was going on. However, I couldn't get through for a long time until 2.30, when Mr. Dusan Nikolic answered. This Mr. Nikolic was the brother of a work colleague of mine. I asked him, "What was going on?" And he said, "It's nothing. Just sleep on it." And I said, "How can I forget about it? We here think that we may go up in the air at any second." And it was only later at that meeting that I heard from Vrkes that it was an orchestrated attack. I told him that people were afraid for real, that somebody might have had a heart attack, somebody could even have got killed, and I told him, "I'm asking you now as a human being, please find me a way. I want to get out of here."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could stop there, witness, and we'll resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Islamcevic, we need to stop here today. We will continue tomorrow afternoon. We are adjourned till tomorrow at 2.15, if I remember well -- 2.15, thank you. In this same courtroom, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 25
